## What you are really learning

Respect the domain's actual contract: randomness, database joins, shell transformations and synchronisation are not one algorithm family.

The goal is not to learn 8 unrelated definitions. Compare the operations needed by each classic problem and notice which invariant survives from one technique to the next.

## Begin with a small example

A stream sample can remain unbiased without storing every element.

$$
P(\text{chosen item after }n)=\frac1n
$$

**What the symbols mean:** P is probability over random replacement decisions and n is the total number of items processed by the one-item reservoir sampler.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For n=3, the first item survives insertion 2 with probability 1/2 and insertion 3 with probability 2/3; multiply to get 1/3. Every item has the same final selection probability.

This is how the topic pages below should be read: understand the numbers first, then generalise to the equation.

## The chapters in this family

1. **[Randomized](../randomized/index.qmd)** — Use random choices inside an algorithm to influence expected performance or output.
2. **[Reservoir Sampling](../reservoir-sampling/index.qmd)** — Maintain a uniform sample from a stream without knowing its final size.
3. **[Rejection Sampling](../rejection-sampling/index.qmd)** — Accept proposed random samples according to a target-to-proposal ratio.
4. **[Design](../design/index.qmd)** — Implement an abstract data type that meets operational contracts and complexity targets.
5. **[Interactive](../interactive/index.qmd)** — Choose queries based on replies while respecting an interaction limit.
6. **[Database](../database/index.qmd)** — Express relational queries and transformations over tables.
7. **[Shell](../shell/index.qmd)** — Compose command-line utilities and streams as processing pipelines.
8. **[Concurrency](../concurrency/index.qmd)** — Reason about overlapping operations, coordination, and shared-state correctness.

## Practice method

Choose ONE chapter. Reproduce its example with paper and pencil, identify what is cached or discarded, implement the tiny idea, and explain one case in which the algorithm's assumptions fail. Repeat until the invariant feels natural.

The [original executable examples](../examples/README.md) provide code you can run and test. If two topics seem similar, compare them in the [algorithm selection guide](../guides/choose-a-pattern.qmd).
